questions.question: The Mosque with "shaking minarets" is situated in which Indian city?
questions.solution:
Sidi Bashir Mosque in Ahmedabad, Gujarat is a former mosque which is also known as the Jhulta Minar or Shaking Minarets. Surviving remains consist of the central gateway and two minarets.

This mosque is believed to be built by either Sidi Bashir (a slave of Ahmed Shah) or by Malik Sarang (a noble in the court of Mahmud Begada) in 1452.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.solution: The SI unit of frequency is Hertz (Hz), named in the memory of the 19th –century German physicist Heinrich Hertz. One hertz means that an event repeats once per second.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded with Padma Shri 2017 in the field of 'Culinary'?
questions.solution: Sanjeev Kapoor was awarded Padma Shri 2017 for his culinary contributions. However, the Padma award lists don’t include a separate category for food. So, Sanjeev Kapoor is listed under the Others-Culinary category.

questions.question: Due to increased weapon launching missions of North Korea, which country has launched a spy satellite to monitor it?
questions.solution: Japan has launched a spy satellite due to North Korea’s increased missile and nuclear programs. A spy satellite, the Radar 5 unit was carried into space on Japan’s mainstay H-IIA rocket. This spy satellite replaced the existing satellite which is approaching the end of its mission.

questions.question: Which of the following has the supreme command of the Indian Defence Forces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__President.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Indian Armed Forces:

 
• The military forces of the Republic of India.
 
• It consists of three professional uniformed services: the Indian Army, Indian Navy, and Indian Air Force. 
 
• Supported by the Indian Coast Guard and paramilitary organizations (Assam Rifles, and Special Frontier Force) and various inter-service commands and institutions such as the Strategic Forces Command, the Andaman and Nicobar Command, and the Integrated Defence Staff.

questions.question: 'The World Outside My Window' is written by ________.
questions.solution:
• ‘The World Outside My Window’ is written by Ruskin Bond, an Indian author of British descent.
 
• In this book, Ruskin Bond writes about some of the most interesting insects, birds, trees, and flowers he has observed.
 
• Ruskin Bond was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992 for ‘**Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra’** in English.
 
• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1999 and Padma Bhushan in 2014.

questions.question: Union Cabinet approves amendments in M-SIPS to attract investment in electronics manufacturing. What is the full form of M-SIPS?
questions.solution:
India’s electronics good import is the third largest import item for the country and to tackle this situation, the central government launched Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme (M-SIPS) in 2012. This scheme is launched to encourage investment and production in the domestic electronic goods sector.

This scheme was modified in 2015, 2016 and 2017.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Banaras Hindu University?
questions.solution: Banaras Hindu University was established by the ‘B.H.U. Act 1915’ in 1916. Madan Mohan Malaviya was the founder of Banaras Hindu University. He was also the Vice-Chancellor of BHU from 1919-1938.

questions.question: With which of the following country, India has a land dispute near Tawang?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**China and India have a land dispute near Tawang in which China especially claims Tawang and other 8 to 10 disputed “hotspot” areas along the Arunachal Pradesh Border.

Some of the disputed areas in Tawang are Namka Chu river valley, Sumdorong Chu, Yangste, and Khizemane.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a connective tissue?
questions.solution:
• The cells of connective tissue are separated from each other and the space between the cells contain matrix. Connective tissues join and support various parts of the body. Cartilage, Bone, and Blood tissues are examples of connective tissues.
 
• Skin is an example of epithelial tissue.

questions.question: Ozone is an ______ of oxygen.
questions.solution:
When a chemical element is present in one or more forms in the same physical state then it is known as allotrope. Swedish scientist Jons Jakob Berzelium proposed the concept of allotropes in 1841.

Ozone (O₃) is an allotrope of oxygen. It is more soluble than oxygen in the water.

Ozone is used for air purification at the crowded places. It is also used in sterilizing drinking water as it oxidizes all germs and bacteria.

questions.question: Which of the following is an Inert Gas?
questions.solution:
An inert gas is a gas that has extremely low reactivity with other substances. The term inert means non-reactive.

Inert gases are also known as noble gases which are placed in group 18 of the periodic table. Inert gases are Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Radon, and Xenon.

questions.question: Soil having high content of aluminum and iron oxide is also known as _______.
questions.solution:
• Pedalfer soil is composed of aluminium and iron oxides. This type of soil is usually found in humid areas.
 
• Pedalfers have three subdivisions of which one is Lateritic soils.

questions.question: When there is only one buyer and one seller of product, it is called ________ situation.
questions.solution:
• Bilateral monopoly is a market structure where there is only one buyer (monopsony) and one seller of a product (monopoly).
 
• When a labor union (monopoly in the supply of labor) faces a single large employer in an industrial town (a monopsonist), it would be an example of a bilateral monopoly.

questions.question: Who was the inventor of frozen foods?
questions.solution: Clarence Birdseye invented a quick-freezing method in 1924 which is responsible for the modern frozen-food industry. This freezing method produces the type of frozen foods that we know today.

questions.question: Convex mirror is generally used in ________.
questions.solution:
Convex mirror is also known as the diverging mirror and the image of the object formed by this mirror is always virtual. The image formed by the mirror is smaller than the size of the object.

Convex mirror is used in sunglasses, as a rear view mirror in vehicles, magnifying glasses, and in telescopes.

questions.question: Red data book contains data of which of the following?
questions.solution:
Red Data Book is a public document which contains the data of endangered and rare species including animals, plants, fungi as well as some local subspecies present in the country.

It was published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. This book is responsible for the evaluation of the total number of wild animals present, identification of all animals and birds and their extinct species.

questions.question: Which among the following sponsors Regional Rural Banks (RRB'S)?
questions.solution:
Regional Rural Banks were established under the provisions of RRB Act 1976. These banks were established to provide sufficient banking and credit facility for agriculture and other rural sectors.

Regional Rural Banks are sponsored by any commercial bank, PSU or private bank. The central government, sponsor bank, and state government have share capital in the ration of 50:35:15.

questions.question: The second Battle of Tarain was fought between ________.
questions.solution:
• The second Battle of Tarain was fought between the army of Mohammed Ghori and Rajput army of Prithviraj Chauhan in 1192 CE. Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Mohammed Ghori.
 
• This battle is regarded as the turning point in India’s history which finally led to the foundation of Delhi Sultanate in 1206 CE.

questions.question: Which among the following is a 'Modifier key'?
questions.solution: Modifier keys are those which are used to enter keyboard shortcuts. When another key is pressed with a modifier key, it modifies the action. Shift, Alt, Control, Command, Function, and Option are the common modifier keys.

questions.question: Anti-defection law is given in which schedule of Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
• Anti-defection law was introduced by the 52ⁿd Amendment in 1985 during the tenure of Rajiv Gandhi. It is given in the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• This law enables the disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection which finally provides a stronger grip to the political parties on their members.
